look_here_first: Start at a mature head and fruit: pappus bristles are plumose to subplumose, with gland-dotted phyllaries. Inspect woody perennial base and leaf nodes, but remember some varieties have alternate rather than opposite leaves. Do not assign a variety from a species-level source row.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial herb to subshrub with woody perennial base; habit varies across recognized varieties.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Leaves usually opposite, but alternate in some varieties including gracillima and texana; phyllotaxy alone cannot reject the species.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Heads discoid; phyllaries gland-dotted, often 22–26 across the complex; involucres roughly 7–15 mm, with about 6–35 florets.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Mature cypsela pappus bristles plumose to subplumose; photograph with macro to distinguish from related brickellbushes.
